newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch fund to use derivatives to enhance returns.
newsitem.headline: Dutch fund to use derivatives to enhance returns.

text.p: PGGM, the second largest pension fund in the Netherlands, plans to use derivatives to enhance the value of its portfolio, chief economist and strategist Marinus Keijzer said on Tuesday.

He told a seminar that PGGM, with 63.5 billion guilders under management for health sector employees, would use derivatives as part of a tactical asset allocation strategy once it reached its desired equities weighting of 55 percent.
But it had not yet started using this technique, which adds to the returns of a portfolio while keeping a "neutral" asset mix, because its current equities exposure was only 45 percent.
PGGM started with no equities in its portfolio in 1983 and aims to reach 55 percent by the end of 1999, which would signal its start of tactical asset allocation.
"The proper use of derivatives is one technique we intend to utilise," he told a seminar on derivatives in funds management at the Amsterdam Derivatives Forum.
After the seminar, Keijzer told Reuters PGGM may even start using this technique in the migration period to the target weighting in shares.
"But our first priority is to get over that level (55 percent)," he said.
The rest of the fund's portfolio is invested in fixed-interest securities and real estate.
As a result of the increased competitiveness of the fund management industry, he told the seminar PGGM had been reallocating assets since 1983 to increase returns.

The planned higher exposure to equities and the relatively small size of the Dutch share market, representing just 1.5 percent of the capitalisation of the world's markets, meant the pension fund had become a major international investor.
With 80 percent of its equity holdings invested offshore, it also faced currency risks that derivatives could curb.
Keijzer said fund managers using derivatives could avoid the large cash-flows and cumbersome processes of investing in the underlying cash markets.
"We are in favour of using an overlay structure that makes it possible to have the best of both possible worlds," he said.
